title: High-Frequency Trading around Large Institutional Orders
one_line: HFTs first trade against large institutional orders (cutting their cost) but then trade with long-lasting orders after ~2-7 hours (raising it): 1 SD of against-flow cuts implementation shortfall 3.4 bps (−46%), 1 SD of with-flow adds 12.5 bps (+169%).

findings.statement: Average implementation shortfall 7.4 bps; HFT against-the-order flow −3.4 bps, with-the-order +12.5 bps per SD.
Pattern fits back-running of informed orders.

why.pattern: Execution mechanics: fast traders detect and ride persistent institutional order flow.

reported_results.headline: HFTs first trade against large institutional orders (cutting their cost) but then trade with long-lasting orders after ~2-7 hours (raising it): 1 SD of against-flow cuts implementation shortfall 3.4 bps (−46%), 1 SD of with-flow adds 12.5 bps (+169%).

tradable_edge: No strategy; supports the order-splitting WHY behind VWAP/drift specs (persistent institutional flow is detectable).
data_fit: Single-stock study — not testable on our ES/NQ data.
caveats: Read by Claude in a chat session (manual run 3), not by the weekly pipeline.
